title: Lumbopelvic ratio L/P vs trunk flexion (10-100% of full ROM)
condition: healthy, standing, forward flexion phase only

quantity.name: lumbopelvic ratio L/P
quantity.definition: total lumbar (T12 vs S1) rotation / total pelvis (S1) rotation at each 10% of full trunk T1 flexion (cumulative ratio, not incremental)

source.sample: 40 young healthy male students, no history of back surgery or recent back/hip/knee complications

protocol.summary: Group mean L/P ratio at 10 trunk-flexion intervals; decreases from 2.96 to 1.07.
how_to_use: Pick the L/P ratio at the task trunk angle (% of full T1 flexion; interpolate).
Given thoracic rotation (≈16-20% of T1, see share test), split the remaining lumbar+pelvis rotation as L = r/(1+r)·(T1−T), P = 1/(1+r)·(T1−T).
Use only for forward flexion; the ratio is cumulative from upright.
equations: L/P = lumbar rotation (T12-S1) / pelvis rotation, both relative to upright (paper's definition)

measurement.device: Xsens MTx inertial sensors (4) on T1, T5, T12 and S1 spinous processes, 100 Hz
measurement.task: slow (4-5 s) forward flexion from neutral upright to maximum voluntary flexion, 3 trials

extraction.from: Fig 2 (left axis); endpoints 2.96 and 1.07 also in Results text
extraction.uncertainty: ±0.02 (217 px per unit at 300 dpi); ±0.03 at 80% and 90% where markers are partly hidden
extraction.check_notes: 10% and 100% match text (2.96, 1.07). 80% and 90% markers partly occluded by other markers; centres reconstructed from visible edge + marker diameter. Cross-check: L/P from digitised lumbar/pelvis curves agrees within 0.03.

pass_rule.rule: input data – not graded; use for robustness checks
